newsitem.title: UK: SMITH & NEPHEW SEES SAME POUND HIT IN H2.
newsitem.headline: SMITH & NEPHEW SEES SAME POUND HIT IN H2.

text.p: British healthcare firm Smith & Nephew said it expected the negative currency impact in the second half to be about as big as in the first half of 1997.
"We are going to see roughly the same sort of impact in the second half as we saw in the first half," chief executive Chris O'Donnell said during a telephone conference.
Smith & Nephew said earlier that the currency hit was 11 million stg in the first six months of the year.
The company cited the pound's strength as the main reason for an 11.75 percent fall in first-half profits to 81.1 million stg.
The dollar's strengthening against several major European major currencies also helped depress results.
